heading: INT. VICTORIAN CONSERVATORY, GLASS WINTER-GARDEN - 1887 - AFTERNOON

units.text: INT. VICTORIAN CONSERVATORY, GLASS WINTER-GARDEN - 1887 - AFTERNOON
Palms press against the glass like prisoners.
A fountain, dry.
Wrought-iron chairs gone green with weather.
LADY CORDELIA WHITTINGTON-BANDELE (30s, bustled gown of dove gray, a face trained to give nothing away) sits with a teacup untasted in her gloved hands.
Across from her, MR. RUPERT ABERNETHY-ODUYA (40s, frock coat, whiskers meticulously combed) turns his hat in his fingers.
By the fountain's rim, partly hidden by a palm, stands MISS PHILIPPA LOVELACE (20s, governess' grey wool, spectacles), who has been told to wait and is waiting.
Lady Cordelia, I must speak plainly.
units.name: RUPERT

units.text: Mr. Abernethy, you have never done otherwise, and I have never thanked you for it.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Then permit me to continue.
units.name: RUPERT

units.text: Permit nothing. Say it.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: He rises.
She rises.
Philippa shrinks behind the palm.
Rupert crosses the tiles in two strides and Cordelia steps back until her skirts catch the iron chair.
It scrapes.
The three of them freeze, an arrangement of statues in a house of glass.
Miss Lovelace, you may go.
units.name: RUPERT

units.text: Yes, sir.
units.name: PHILIPPA

units.text: No, Philippa. Stay.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Cordelia--
units.name: RUPERT

units.text: Mr. Abernethy, whatever you have to say about the letters, you may say before my governess. She wrote them.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Philippa lifts her chin.
The palm leaves stir, though there is no wind.
Rupert's hat slips from his hand and rolls, round and round, to the dry fountain's edge.
